A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FuncGenFoil work. Their complete 11-page contents, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original airfoil generation and editing experiments, kernel and initialization ablations, and aerodynamic simulations of generated CRM wings.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental and simulation outcomes, including Tables 1–5 and Figures 5–7.

M1.justification: The Fourier neural operator, flow-matching objective, Gaussian-process initialization, ODE generation, and MAP-based editing procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–3 are retained; newly discussed neural operators appear only as related work.

E1.justification: Both versions use UIUC, Super, AF-200K, and CRM geometries for the same generation, editing, resolution-transfer, and aerodynamic evaluation scenarios. The added discussion of unlabeled engineering data does not introduce evaluated data or tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains CVAE, CGAN, PK-VAE, PK-GAN, PKVAE-GAN, and PK-DIT as AF-200K comparators, with PK-DIT comparisons on UIUC and Super. No newly cited method receives a reported comparison.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, training budgets, and testing procedures are unchanged. Both retain 300 editing cases, training resolution 257 with evaluation at 513 and 1025, and aerodynamic evaluation of 500 generated wings after training on 135,000 CRM geometries.

E4.justification: The kernel/FNO-mode ablation, ODE-inversion versus zero-initialization ablation, resolution analysis, and editing and aerodynamic examples are unchanged. Section 4.3 adds theoretical discussion without adding an ablation or other empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting and averaging over editing cases. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and Figures 5–7 retain identical results. For example, AF-200K mean label error remains 255 in units of 10^-3, diversity remains -71.6, and Table 2 editing MSE remains 2.41–2.75 × 10^-7.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 newly states a theoretical condition, attributed to Lim et al. (2025): noise must be at least d/2 less regular than data to ensure data-space containment in the noise space. Existing equations and the MAP derivation remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain their claims about function-space representation, arbitrary-resolution generation, airfoil editing, and generation quality. The headline 74.4% label-error reduction and 23.2% diversity increase are unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 supplements the empirical preference for smoother kernels with an explanation involving noise/data regularity and the Matérn smoothness parameter. Section 2 also newly argues that engineering data scarcity favors generative models capable of using unlabeled or untested designs.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices A–C retain the same hardware, hyperparameters, ODE-step choices, angular-fitting qualification, and optimal-transport implementation disclosure. Both versions still state that code will be released.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Lipman et al. (2024), Liu-Schiaffini et al. (2024), Zeng et al. (2025), Su et al. (2020), and Kirillov et al. (2023), modestly expanding research context. Lim et al. (2025), already cited in v1, gains a specific theoretical discussion.

P1.justification: Changes consist of localized prose expansion and rewriting in Section 2 and an added discussion in Section 4.3. The title, main narrative, section sequence, and appendix organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing displays move with text reflow: Figure 2 shifts from page 3 to 4, Figures 3–4 from page 4 to 5, Table 4 from page 7 to 8, and Algorithm 2 from page 10 to 11. Graphics, captions, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves contextualization by discussing localized and point-cloud neural operators and connecting kernel choice to a specific noise/data regularity condition. These additions help readers understand the modeling rationale, while the method, empirical evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, limiting the overall gain.
